beats.chip: Cold open — too strong / too weak
beats.visual: Cinematic cold open on a desaturated chemical drum; three warnings type on (too strong, too weak, nobody measured) as a cyan iris tries to open over the drum and fails.
beats.script: Mix a cleaning chemical too strong, and it eats your equipment and burns your people. Mix it too weak, and it leaves behind the very bacteria it was meant to kill. And the worst part? Nobody sees the mistake — not until the audit, the injury, or the recall.
agentNotes: needs motion scene: cold-open drum (grey → warnings type on) + iris that tries to open and fails — full-bleed bookend, no phone still

beats.visual: The iris opens for real over the drum snapping to full colour; the CCV title and 'a second pair of eyes' tagline resolve; the station-list phone journey pans in at the tail.
beats.script: This is Chemical Concentration Verification — we call it C-C-V. Think of it as a second pair of eyes. At every drum, every satellite, every dilution point. It doesn't trust the label, and it doesn't trust your memory. It measures.
agentNotes: needs motion scene: iris opens (two blinks) + drum desaturated→colour + CCV title reveal; phone (station-list-top.png) pans in as the tail transition

beats.visual: Issue screen: the scope control at the top of the phone is ringed as the operator chooses Entire Factory vs a single Department; the choice then travels onto the record.
beats.script: Before anything is measured, you make one choice. Who is this issue for? The entire factory, or a single department. That choice travels with the record. So every dilution is tied to exactly where it was used.

beats.visual: Verify screen with the approved-range hero ringed; the Chemical Matrix card (chemical, method, approved range, reference) seals shut with a lock — the standard is set before anyone touches a station.
beats.script: Before anyone touches a station, the standard is already set. Each chemical's spec lives in the Matrix — its approved range, and the one test method that proves it. The operator's job is simple. Measure, and read. Never to decide what "correct" means.

beats.chip: Manual issue — chemical + water, % calculated live
beats.visual: Manual dilution: enter litres of chemical + water; the computed dilution hero (ringed) turns coral out of range, emerald in range; then the app pushes 'verify now'.
beats.script: In manual mode, you enter the chemical, and the water you used. The app calculates the dilution percentage live, checking it against the approved range as you go. And once you record it, the app doesn't just leave it open. It pushes you to veryfy now — while you're still standing at the station.
agentNotes: CcvTutorial crossfades issue-scope-factory → issue-manual-outofrange → issue-manual-inrange across this beat; still binds the in-range end state

beats.visual: Satellite / auto-dosing issue screen: the litres-issued field is ringed (amber); no water field — the pump doses downstream; a fresh batch is flagged NEEDS VERIFY until proven.
beats.script: Satellite and auto-dosing stations are different. They skip dilution at issue time completely — the pump handles that downstream. So you just record the chemical litres issued to the station. And verification is tracked per dosing station, not per issue. A fresh batch still gets flagged — until it's been proven.

beats.visual: A fake 'select test method' dropdown appears, then shatters into shards to reveal there is no dropdown — the Matrix already locked the method (Titration drops).
beats.script: Here's what most people get wrong. You'd expect the operator to choose a test method. They don't. There's no dropdown. The Matrix already decided — titration drops, conductivity, or a test strip, depending on the chemical. The operator just walks up, and the correct test is already waiting.
agentNotes: needs motion scene: fake method dropdown builds then shatters (6-shard clip-path throw) revealing the locked method label; verify-blank.png sits in the phone underneath

beats.visual: The verify screen morphs through each test method (drops / microstainer / ppm / percent / visual / conductivity) against a constant spec hero, with a method rail checking off; ends on repeat-verification checkpoints across the shift.
beats.script: The veryfy screen adapts to the chemical. Titration drops, a conductivity reading, or a test strip — same screen, whichever one the Matrix chose. Three methods, always the right one for that chemical. Conductivity can even auto-fill the shift's plant-water baseline. And it doesn't stop at one check — concentration can be proven again and again, start to finish.
agentNotes: needs motion scene: fully-composed shapeshifter — no captured still; input card flips per method against a constant SpecHero + a method gate rail; ends on a repeat-verify checkpoint strip

beats.chip: Out of spec — corrective action + retest
beats.visual: Out-of-spec reading: the Complete Verification button is padlocked (ringed coral) until a corrective action and a re-test are captured; then it unlocks and the record shows both the miss and the recovery.
beats.script: Out of spec doesn't end in blame. The app simply refuses to move on. It demands a corrective action, and a re-test, before the button even unlocks. So you fix it. You test again. And if it passes? It's resolved on the spot. The record shows both the miss and the recovery.
agentNotes: CcvTutorial crossfades verify-outofspec.png → verify-retest-passed.png; still binds the out-of-spec state where the locked button lives

beats.visual: Re-test still failing: the operator's button becomes Record & Escalate (ringed coral); a cyan thread carries the NCR to the site manager's own device, who acknowledges and signs.
beats.script: What if the re-test fails too? One operator shouldn't carry that alone. So the app raises a non-conformance and names the site manager. The button becomes Record and Escalate. On their own device, the manager acknowledges, and signs. Accountability travels up the chain — automatically.
agentNotes: operator phone anchors on verify-escalation-btn.png; the site-manager device + cyan handoff thread are composed (bespoke) — TutorialKit renders the still + escalation ring only

beats.visual: Airplane-mode floor: three actions save locally with a buzz and drop into an offline queue; when signal returns they run like a relay in strict order through a clientOpId sync gate, temp IDs swap for real, and a duplicate retry is turned away.
beats.script: Factory floors have dead spots. CCV doesn't care. Offline, every action saves instantly — with a buzz — then waits in a queue. When the signal returns, they run like a relay, in strict order. Temporary IDs are swapped for real ones. And a retry that tries to submit twice is turned away. Nothing lost. Nothing doubled.
agentNotes: needs motion scene: fully-composed relay — no captured still; action chips fire → batons drop into an offline queue rail → run through a clientOpId sync gate on reconnect → duplicate baton bounced

beats.visual: Recap bookend: a 2×2 grid of the real stills with the iris travelling across them, then dissolve to the coloured drum with the three takeaways and the 'second pair of eyes' close on the e-wizer + Ecowize lockup.
beats.script: Three things to hold onto. The Matrix owns the standard. The station mode owns the flow. And verification is what makes a dilution provable. Fail, and the app walks you through re-test and escalation — automatically. Offline, nothing is lost. A second pair of eyes on every drum. One that never blinks first.
